question:
A bounded feasible region has corner points $O(0,0)$, $A(6,0)$, $B(4,4)$ and $C(0,6)$. For the objective function $Z=x+2y$, use the corner point method to:
(i) find the maximum value of $Z$;
(ii) determine whether the optimal feasible solution is unique. Give reason.
explanation:
Step 1: Evaluating $Z$ at $O$ and $A$
Using $Z=x+2y$, $$Z_O=0+2(0)=0$$ and $$Z_A=6+2(0)=6$$
Step 2: Evaluating $Z$ at $B$ and $C$
At $B(4,4)$, $$Z_B=4+2(4)=12$$ At $C(0,6)$, $$Z_C=0+2(6)=12$$
Step 3: Determining the maximum
The greatest corner-point value is $$Z_{\max}=12$$ and it occurs at both $B$ and $C$.
Step 4: Examining uniqueness
Since two distinct corner points give the same maximum value, the optimal feasible solution is not unique.
Step 5: Applying the multiple-optimum result
Every point on the line segment joining two optimal corner points also gives the same optimal value.
Step 6: Conclusion
Thus, the maximum value is $12$, and every feasible point on the segment $BC$ is an optimal feasible solution.

options.A:
(i) Maximum value $12$
(ii) The optimum is not unique; every point on segment $BC$ is optimal
options.B:
(i) Maximum value $12$
(ii) The unique optimum is $B(4,4)$
options.C:
(i) Maximum value $10$
(ii) The optimum is not unique at $A$ and $C$
options.D:
(i) Maximum value $16$
(ii) The unique optimum is $C(0,6)$
